units.text: Do not acquire the reproaches of evil men or imitate their ways,
for every lawless person is unclean before the Lord, and he does not sit in council among the righteous.
God’s curse is in the houses of the ungodly, but the dwellings of the righteous are blessed.
The Lord opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
The wise will inherit glory, but the ungodly raised up dishonor.

In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, so that the Lord’s word through Jeremiah’s mouth might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians. He ordered a proclamation throughout his kingdom, also in writing, saying:
“Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: The Lord, God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has charged me to build Him a house in Jerusalem in Judea.
Who among you belongs to any of His people? His God will be with him, and he will go up to Jerusalem in Judea. Let him build the house of the God of Israel—He is the God in Jerusalem.

As for everyone left behind, from whatever place he resides in, the men of his place will take him up with silver, gold, belongings and livestock, together with the freewill offering for the house of God in Jerusalem.”
The leaders of the families of Judah and Benjamin, the priests and the Levites arose, of all those whose spirit God had stirred to go up and build the Lord’s house in Jerusalem.
All those around them strengthened their hands with silver vessels, gold, belongings, livestock and gifts of hospitality, apart from the freewill offerings.
I mean not your own conscience, but the other’s. For why is my freedom judged by another conscience?
If I partake with thanksgiving, why am I slandered for what I give thanks for?
Therefore, whether you eat or drink or do anything, do everything for God’s glory.
Give no cause for stumbling to Jews or Greeks or the Church of God,
just as I too please everyone in everything, seeking not my own benefit but that of the many, so that they may be saved.
With what shall I take hold of the Lord and grasp my God Most High? Shall I take hold of Him with whole burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
Will the Lord receive with thousands of rams or with ten thousands of fat-rich torrents? Shall I give my firstborn offspring for impieties, the fruit of my body for the sin of my life?
Has it been declared to you, O man, what is good? Or what does the Lord seek from you, except to do justice, and to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with the Lord your God?
Wisdom is celebrated at the exits, and in the squares she speaks openly.
At the tops of walls she is proclaimed; at rulers’ gates she sits nearby, and at city gates she speaks boldly:
As long as the innocent hold to righteousness, they will not be ashamed. But the senseless, desiring insolence, became ungodly and hated perception,
and became liable to reproofs. Behold, I will send forth to you an utterance of my breath, and I will teach you my word.

And it shall be, as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so shall the Lord rejoice over you to destroy you; and you shall be removed from the land whither you go to inherit it.

And the Lord your God shall scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth unto the other; and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone, which neither you nor your fathers have known.

And among those nations He shall give you no rest, neither shall there be a resting place for the sole of your foot; and the Lord shall give you there a faint heart, and failing eyes, and a wasting soul.
And your life shall hang before your eyes, and you shall fear day and night, and shall have no assurance of your life.

In the morning you shall say: Would that it were evening! And at evening you shall say: Would that it were morning! Because of the fear of your heart wherewith you shall fear, and the sights of your eyes which you shall see.
You will recognize that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion on My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a holy city, and foreigners will no longer pass through her.
On that day mountains will drip sweetness, hills will flow with milk, and all Judah’s water outlets will flow with water. A spring will come out of the Lord’s house and water the Wadi of Rushes.
For heaven will be new and earth new, and they will never remember former things, nor will those things enter their heart,
but they will find joy and exultation in it. For behold, I am making Jerusalem an exultation and My people joy.
I will exult over Jerusalem and rejoice over My people, and no sound of weeping or crying will ever again be heard in her.

There will never be one cut off prematurely there, nor an old man who fails to complete his time. For the young person will be a hundred years old, but the sinner who dies will be a hundred years old and accursed.
They will build houses and inhabit them themselves; they will plant vineyards and eat their own produce.
They will not build for others to inhabit or plant for others to eat. For My people’s days will be like those of the tree of life; they will wear out the works of their labor.
My chosen ones will not labor in vain or bear children for a curse, because they are offspring blessed by God, and their descendants will be with them.
Daughter Zion’s elders sat on the ground in silence. They put dust on their heads and girded themselves with sackcloth. They brought the leading virgins in Jerusalem down to the ground.
My eyes failed with tears; my heart was troubled. My glory was poured onto the ground at the shattering of the daughter of my people, as infant and nursing child failed in the city’s squares.
They said to their mothers, “Where are grain and wine?” They weakened like the wounded in the city’s squares, and their lives poured out into their mothers’ bosoms.
And the Lord said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh within herself, saying, ‘Shall I indeed bear a child, though I have grown old?’
Is any word impossible with God? At this season I will return to you, when the time comes round; and Sarah shall have a son.”
After giving the purchase document to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the Lord:
O Lord, Thou madest heaven and earth by Thy great strength and Thy high, uplifted arm. Nothing can be hidden from Thee.
But now thus says the Lord God who made you, Jacob, who formed you, Israel: “Do not fear, for I redeemed you. I called you by your name; you are Mine.
Even if you cross through water, I am with you, and rivers will not flood over you. Even if you pass through fire, you will certainly not be burned up; flame will not burn you up.
For I am the Lord your God, Israel’s Holy One, who saves you. I made Egypt your exchange, and Ethiopia and Soene on your behalf.
Since you became honored before Me, you were glorified, and I loved you. I will give many people on your behalf and rulers for your head.
Do not fear, for I am with you. From the east I will bring your offspring, and from the west I will gather you.
I will say to the north, ‘Bring them,’ and to the southwest, ‘Do not hinder. Bring My sons from a distant land and My daughters from the earth’s extremities,
all who are called by My name.’ For in My glory I fashioned him, formed him, and made him,
Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,

not according to the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took their hand to bring them out of Egypt’s land, because they did not remain in My covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.

Because this is the covenant I will make with Israel’s house after those days, says the Lord: I will surely put My laws into their understanding and write them upon their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be My people.

And they will certainly not teach each his fellow citizen or his brother, saying, Know the Lord, because they will all know Me, from their least to their greatest. I will be merciful toward their injustices and certainly remember their sins no more.

You sowed much and brought in little; you ate, but were not satisfied; you drank, but not to intoxication; you clothed yourselves, but were not warmed in them. The one gathering wages gathered them into a bundle with holes.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Place your hearts upon your ways.
Go up onto the mountain, cut wood and rebuild the house. I will take pleasure in it and be glorified, said the Lord.

You looked for much, and it came to little; it was brought into the house, and I blew it away. Therefore, thus says the Lord Almighty: Because My house is desolate, while each of you hurries to his own house,
therefore heaven will hold back dew, and the earth will withhold its produce.
I will bring a sword upon the land and the mountains, upon grain, wine and oil, and whatever the earth produces, upon people and livestock, and upon all the labors of their hands.”
If you walk in My ordinances, keep My commandments, and do them,
then I will give you rain in its season. The land shall yield its produce, and the trees of the fields shall yield their fruit.
And your threshing shall reach the grape harvest, and the grape harvest shall reach the sowing. You shall eat your bread to satisfaction and dwell securely in your land.
And war shall not pass through your land. I will give peace in your land. You shall lie down, with no one to frighten you, and I will destroy harmful animals from your land.
And the Lord said to Abram, “Go out from your land, and from your kindred, and from your father’s house, to the land that I will show you.
And I will make you a great nation, and I will bless you and make your name great; and you shall be blessed.
And I will bless those who bless you, and those who curse you I will curse; and in you all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed.”
I am gathering them from all the land where I scattered them in My anger, wrath, and great indignation. I will bring them back to this place and settle them in confidence.
They will be My people, and I will be their God.
I will give them another way and another heart, to fear Me always, for their good and their children’s good after them.
I will establish an eternal covenant with them, which I will certainly not turn back from behind them. I will put My fear in their heart so that they do not depart from Me.
I will attend to them to do them good and will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all heart and all soul.
For thus said the Lord: Just as I brought all these great calamities upon this people, so I will bring upon them all the good things I spoke concerning them.
Therefore, putting away falsehood, let each speak truth with his neighbor, because we are members of one another.
“What benefit is there in my blood, in my descending into corruption? Will dust give thanks unto Thee, or announce Thy truth?”
The Lord heard and had mercy on me; the Lord became my helper.
Thou didst turn my lament into dancing for me; Thou didst tear open my sackcloth and gird me with gladness,
so that my glory may sing praise unto Thee, and I may certainly not be pierced with grief. Lord my God, I will thank Thee for ever.
The word that came from the Lord to Isaiah son of Amos concerning Judea and Jerusalem.
In the last days the Lord’s mountain and God’s house will be clearly visible on the summits of the mountains and be raised above the hills; all the nations will come to it,

and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

He will judge between the nations and reprove a numerous people. They will beat their swords into plows and their spears into sickles. Nation will no longer take sword against nation, and they will certainly no longer learn to wage war.

Thus says the Lord Sabaoth: “Egypt toiled, and the Ethiopians’ trade; and the Seboin, tall men, will cross over to you and become your slaves. They will follow behind you, bound with handcuffs, bow to you, and pray in you, because God is in you. They will say, ‘There is no God besides Thee;
